current.text: He is a locked-in starter for New Orleans, next to Dejounte Murray and Zion Williamson.
Much of his production last season came while Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones and Jordan Poole were out. Over the last 15 games, with Murray back, his usage fell to 20 and he averaged under 20 points.
Experts disagree on his role. Most expect less usage with Murray running the offense and possibly fewer than 36 minutes. Lloyd does not believe his role is unstable.

Experts disagree on his category-league price. One calls him a fade with fair value in the 40s. Another says pick 28 is justifiable. Lloyd would take him around pick 20. Josh says he has slid too far and is worth mid 20s USD; he paid 21 USD in a mock auction and called it good value.
One expert doubts that his 1.5 steals and his field goal percentage will hold, and questions whether he gets to the line enough.
His trade value is at its peak because of his team-friendly contract. The Pelicans reportedly want about three first-round picks and a young player for him.

The Pelicans roster is crowded with high-usage players: Murray, Zion, second-year Jeremiah Fears, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Yves Missi, Derik Queen and the added Bennedict Mathurin. Splitting the minutes is hard to project.
The team lacks shooting, and he is basically its only floor spacer.
Jamahl Mosley is the new head coach and brings a defense-first identity.
Experts see the Pelicans as a weak team near the bottom of the West. One projects about 34 wins and no playoffs.
The Pelicans do not control their own draft pick because of a swap with Atlanta and Milwaukee. That gave them a reason to keep winning late last season.
With a season end on March 28, New Orleans plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks, which is a good schedule.
New Orleans has a league-high 16 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is worth clearly more in category leagues than in points leagues. Last season he finished 22nd in category leagues and 43rd in points leagues.

note: Murphy has no weak category and is strong in threes, FT% on volume, points and steals, so he fits any build. The fight is over price: Yahoo values him at 30 USD, ESPN at 12 USD, and he cost 20 USD in our league last season. The low 20s USD that Josh and our past auction point to looks fair. Above 25 USD you are paying for last season's role, which came with Murray out. Early in the season, check his usage and minutes next to Murray (36 minutes last season) and whether his steal rate holds near 1.5.
